What is Eid Mubarak’s meaning?‘Eid Mubarak’ is often used as a greeting, similar to how you would wish somebody ‘Merry Christmas’, or ‘Happy Hanukkah’. ‘Eid’ refers to a feast, festival or celebration, while ‘Mubarak’ means ‘blessed’ – together, it translates to ‘Blessed Celebration’, or ‘Blessed Feast’.What is the difference between Eid and Eid Mubarak?Eid al-Fitr refers to the Muslim holiday that celebrates the end of Ramadan. Whereas Eid al-Adah refers to the Feast of Sacrifice, which is often celebrated a couple of months after Eid al-Fitr.‘Eid Mubarak’ is a message which can be used in cards, messages and social posts for both occasions to show people you’re thinking of them.When can I say Eid Mubarak?You can say ‘Eid Mubarak’ when you want to wish someone in the Muslim community a Happy Eid. It’s a saying that’s usually said when greeting someone or sending a celebratory message – for example, in a card.Is Adobe Express free?Yes, our free plan offers many core features including thousands of templates, photo editing and effects, animation, and 2GB of storage.
